title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measure whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated repair budget increases the probability that an LLM‑produced network‑change proposal passes semantic validation versus accepting the same single LLM candidate without repair. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents stratified by difficulty (100 per stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic semantic validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial candidate that was evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (run deterministic validation and allow ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.996667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and a one‑edit repair budget the generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue to a single sequencing omission that the permitted edit corrected. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts; interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policy choices.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment change proposals, operational correctness requires satisfying semantic invariants (sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation) that superficially correct syntax or templates do not guarantee. A common engineering pattern is generate→validate→repair: pair a generative model with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair to reduce deployment risk. However, the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on the chosen estimand (what is held fixed), the single‑shot quality of the generator, the validator's semantic coverage, and the permitted repair budget. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment designed to isolate deterministic rescue that arises from applying a verifier and a bounded repair operator to the identical single LLM candidate per intent. The primary research question is: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating the bounded, post‑generation verifier/repair effect under a shared_initial estimand; (2) a complete archived execution and analysis bundle with validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of ceiling effects, estimand conditioning, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work: Prior work documents active application of LLMs to NetOps tasks and highlights tradeoffs when integrating external tools and validators. Surveys and system papers report progress in intent translation, configuration synthesis, automated test generation, and repair, and they emphasize that deterministic checks or tool‑augmented agentic frameworks (planner‑centric or ReAct‑style) can improve output correctness provided the tools' semantics match deployment invariants [1,2,3]. Empirical reports of generate→validate→repair pipelines show variable improvements that depend on validator expressiveness and whether pipelines permit resampling or iterative regeneration; conflating deterministic validation with benefits derived from resampling complicates attribution of improvement to the verifier itself [3,4]. Separate literature on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets proposes detectors and guardrails that can reduce false positives but whose effectiveness depends on the threat model and validator coverage [5]. Work combining symbolic fault localization or formal verification with generative repair operators reports promising but task‑dependent gains, suggesting hybrid designs merit head‑to‑head study under carefully specified estimands [6,7]. Our study follows calls in the literature to specify estimands clearly and to evaluate verifier benefit under operationally realistic model‑call budgets.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 and froze the confirmatory estimand: the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents after pre‑specified inclusion/exclusion rules (preregistration SHA‑256 archived). Design and sampling. Tasks were deterministically generated into a synthetic topology suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). Each task encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final states, sequencing constraints, preserve‑state invariants, and protected interfaces. Confirmatory sampling drew 100 paired intents per stratum. Shared_initial protocol and generator. To isolate deterministic rescue from resampling benefits we used a shared_initial estimand: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate from the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) which was reused verbatim in both baseline and guarded evaluations. Validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule that checks sequencing, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded in the suite, and protected‑interface templates. The guarded pipeline allowed at most one automated repair attempt per pair implemented as a constrained, localized edit operator (insertion or small reordering to fix sequencing omissions). Repair attempts were applied only when the validator flagged the shared_initial candidate and were re‑validated deterministically. Contamination and missingness controls. The preregistration included negative controls and deterministic contamination checks; pairs would be excluded only if both pipeline calls for the pair failed due to infrastructure/provider outage. Analysis executor. The confirmatory analysis used a paired binary test executor (exact McNemar two‑sided) and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with seed = 1729 and B = 10000. Secondary and stratum tests were designated exploratory and subject to multiplicity control where reported.
sections.results: Execution integrity and counts. The preregistered adapter completed the confirmatory run under the shared_initial protocol, producing 300 complete paired observations. Model‑call accounting: 301 model calls were used (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair call). No pairs were excluded, and no provider/infrastructure dual‑call outages occurred. Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300, i.e., baseline = 299/300 (0.996667) and guarded = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) = [0.00, 0.01]. Per‑stratum diagnostics. Low and medium strata were at ceiling under both conditions (100/100 each). The single discordant pair resided in the high difficulty stratum (baseline 99/100, guarded 100/100). Repair trace. The solitary guarded rescue invoked the permitted single edit: the shared_initial candidate omitted a required 'admin down' sequencing step; a constrained insertion repair corrected the omission and the deterministic validator reported a valid pass after the edit. Contamination and negative controls. Deterministic contamination checks and negative controls produced no unexpected passes. Cost and operational footprint. Under this design the deterministic rescue required a single additional repair stage call across 300 pairs, indicating low marginal model‑call cost for bounded repair in this synthetic suite. Statistical interpretation. The inferential result (p = 1.0) reflects minimal discordance (m = n10 + n01 = 1) under a near‑ceiling baseline, yielding limited statistical power to detect small absolute improvements; the paired bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.
sections.discussion: Estimand and operational relevance. The shared_initial estimand models operational policies that limit model calls (cost, latency, governance). Under such a policy the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to the identical candidate. Alternative operational choices—allowing resampling, iterative verifier‑guided regeneration, or larger iterative repair budgets—change the estimand and typically increase achievable pass rates. Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration included an optional calibration pilot to estimate discordance and refine power; that pilot was not executed. As a result the main run confronted a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300), producing minimal discordance and low sensitivity to small absolute effects. This outcome highlights the practical value of small pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling for chosen tasks. Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The single failure mode observed was a sequencing omission; other semantic classes (reachability violations or forbidden ACL edits) were not prevalent in this synthetic suite. The guarded pipeline's marginal utility scales with (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness: richer validators that check more semantic properties can increase observable rescue rates but demand commensurate specification and verification engineering. Repair budget tradeoffs. We intentionally limited automated repair to one constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue; iterative or more permissive repair operators would likely increase rescue but constitute a different operational policy and estimand. Reproducibility and artifact availability. We archive the preregistration, task manifests, validator traces, repair transcript for the rescued episode, execution logs, and analysis inputs to permit deterministic replay and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distributions, or repair budgets.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation that conditioned on a single shared LLM draw per intent, adding a deterministic validator plus at most one constrained automated repair produced one deterministic rescue across 300 paired intents (baseline 299/300, guarded 300/300). The absolute paired improvement was 0.00333 with exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 and a 95% paired bootstrap CI of [0.00, 0.01]. The principal practical conclusion is conditional: under operational policies that limit model calls and under the evaluated synthetic task distribution, a bounded verifier+repair mechanism can deterministically rescue some sequencing omissions at negligible extra model‑call cost, but when the single‑shot generator is near ceiling the observable marginal benefit is small. We release the preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to enable reproducible follow‑ups that change estimand conditioning, enlarge repair budgets, or evaluate alternative validator expressiveness.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or to validators with different semantic coverage.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended to estimate discordance for power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or interactive regeneration).

Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; iterative or more permissive repair strategies would constitute a different estimand and may yield different outcomes.
